# ankra_managed_service (Resource)

A managed service set up from a service package on a cluster, the counterpart of `ankra services setup` and `ankra services retire`. Setting it up reviews the plan and confirms it straight away (the platform's review is valid for ten minutes), then waits until the service is serving. A failed install fails the apply; a wait that runs out (`timeouts.create`) only warns, and the service is kept in state while its install goes on.

A managed service cannot be changed in place: changing any set-up input replaces it, which retires the old service first. **Retiring a service deletes its data** (its stack, namespace, volumes and secrets). Destroy, and so any replacement, therefore refuses unless `allow_data_loss_on_destroy` is `true`; set it, apply, then destroy.

The inputs are read back, so one changed outside Terraform (for example a service moved to another package version with the CLI) also plans a replacement, which the guard refuses. Update the configuration to the service's current value (`ankra_services` shows it) to keep the service, or allow the data loss to replace it.

The platform does not return `consumer_ids`, `parameters` or `secret_references`, so they are kept as configured and are null after an import. Consumers connected later, outside Terraform, show in `connected_consumer_ids` and are disconnected when the service is retired.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "ankra_service_packages" "all" {}

resource "ankra_service_placement_policy" "prod" {
  cluster_id    = "9f4c2d1e-5a6b-4c7d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f"
  region        = "eu-north-1"
  data_boundary = "eu"
}

resource "ankra_service_consumer" "orders" {
  application_id = "3c2b1a0f-9e8d-4c7b-a6f5-e4d3c2b1a0f9"
  cluster_id     = ankra_service_placement_policy.prod.cluster_id
  namespace      = "orders"
}

resource "ankra_managed_service" "orders_db" {
  package_version_id = one([for package in data.ankra_service_packages.all.packages : package.id if package.name == "postgres" && package.version == "1.0.0"])
  name               = "orders-db"
  cluster_id         = ankra_service_placement_policy.prod.cluster_id
  region             = ankra_service_placement_policy.prod.region
  data_boundary      = ankra_service_placement_policy.prod.data_boundary
  consumer_ids       = [ankra_service_consumer.orders.id]

  # Retiring the service deletes its data. Destroy (and replacement) refuse
  # until this is set to true.
  allow_data_loss_on_destroy = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster the service runs on. It needs a declared placement policy (`ankra_service_placement_policy`).
- `data_boundary` (String) Data boundary; it must equal the data boundary of the cluster's placement policy.
- `name` (String) Service name: lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, starting with a letter, at most 63 characters. Unique in the organisation.
- `package_version_id` (String) Service package version to set the service up from (`ankra_service_packages`).
- `region` (String) Region; it must equal the region of the cluster's placement policy.

### Optional

- `allow_data_loss_on_destroy` (Boolean) Allow destroy (and replacement) to retire the service, which deletes its data. Defaults to `false`, which makes destroy fail without touching the service.
- `consumer_ids` (Set of String) Consumer bindings (`ankra_service_consumer`) to connect the service to at setup, at most 100.
- `mode` (String) `customer` (the default) runs the service on the cluster; `existing` adopts one already there.
- `parameters` (Map of Number) Integer parameters the package takes, at most 32.
- `secret_references` (Map of String) Secrets the package takes, by name (such as `ADMIN_PASSWORD`), each the id of a credential grant. At most 16.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `wait_until_ready` (Boolean) Wait at setup until the service is serving (or deployed). Defaults to `true`; a failed install then fails the apply.

### Read-Only

- `cluster_name` (String) Name of the cluster.
- `connected_consumer_ids` (Set of String) Consumer bindings the service is connected to now.
- `created_at` (String) When the service was set up.
- `generation` (Number) Generation of the service; every change increases it.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the service (the id of the review it was set up from).
- `readiness` (String) Readiness the platform last observed.
- `state` (String) `deploying`, `deployed`, `serving`, `degraded`, `failed`, `retiring` or `unknown`.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Managed services are imported by service id (ankra services list).
terraform import ankra_managed_service.orders_db 6a5b4c3d-2e1f-4a0b-9c8d-7e6f5a4b3c2d
```
